_note: Exposure history -> risk -> what to monitor, as NASA's Lifetime Surveillance of Astronaut Health does (an exposure history per astronaut, monitoring per hazard). 'monitoring' = from the cited sources; 'our_plan' = our step that follows from the risk, not stated in a source.

previous_spaceflight.label: Previous spaceflights
previous_spaceflight.risk: Radiation from every spaceflight adds up. NASA limits an astronaut's total career dose from spaceflight to less than 600 mSv, for all ages and sexes.
monitoring: Add this mission's dose to the career total and keep it below 600 mSv

long_duration_flight.label: Previous long-duration flight
long_duration_flight.risk: About 70% of long-duration crewmembers show signs of SANS, changes in the eye and optic nerve, from mild to severe. No permanent loss of vision has been seen.
monitoring: Vision screening, retinal photography, OCT and eye ultrasound before flight, on flight days 30 and 90, and after flight
our_plan: Compare the eye images with those from the previous flight

aircraft_pilot.label: Years as a jet pilot
aircraft_pilot.risk: US astronauts have more melanoma than expected (2.5 times), consistent with what is seen in aircraft pilots. The authors suggest ultraviolet light or lifestyle, not spaceflight itself.
our_plan: Skin check for new or changing moles before and after the mission

outdoor_work.label: Years of outdoor work in the sun
outdoor_work.risk: Outdoor work in sunlight raises the risk of sunburn and skin cancer.
our_plan: Skin check for new or changing moles before and after the mission
Sun protection during field training on Earth

noise.label: Noisy workplace (engines, machinery)
noise.risk: Noise exposure is generally considered to affect hearing. Temporary and some permanent hearing loss has been documented after long spaceflights, though a clear link to station noise is not proven.
monitoring: Personal audio devices are limited to 115 dBA at the ear on board
our_plan: Hearing test before and after the mission (hearing tests on board are disturbed by noise)

bone_predisposition.label: Family history of osteoporosis or a previous fracture
bone_predisposition.risk: Astronauts can lose up to 1-2% of bone density per month in the hip and spine, compared with 0.5-1% per year in older people on Earth.
monitoring: Bone scan (DXA) before and after spaceflight
Biochemical samples before, during and after flight

insomnia_history.label: History of insomnia
insomnia_history.risk: Astronauts sleep less in space than on the ground, and short sleep is linked to more mistakes and slower decisions.
monitoring: Wrist monitor for activity and light (actigraphy)
our_plan: Protect the sleep window in busy weeks
